title: Rav Yehoshua
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pesachim 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.53b): “Rav Yehoshua said: Rava expounded.” Perhaps he was the father of the well-known Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. Dikdukei Soferim records an omission at “Rav Yehoshua.” In [Shabbat 151b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b) we find: “Rabbi Levi said: Rabbi Pappi said: Rabbi Yehoshua said: After three days his belly splits open,” etc. There the reading should be Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin, as explained in his entry.[^1]

notes.text: The proposed father-son identification and the correction to Yehoshua of Sikhnin are Hyman’s, with “perhaps” preserved. The contextual patronymic in רב הונא בריה דר״י is expanded as Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua without assigning an external identity. דק״ס is the customary abbreviation for Dikdukei Soferim. Hyman writes ליתא תיבת רב יהושע; this may concern the complete designation or just Rav before Yehoshua. “An omission at” avoids the earlier English’s unjustified restriction to Rav alone while leaving the exact extent unresolved. The repeated א״ר clauses are kept as successive “said” attributions; no additional transmission links are supplied. The pronoun “his” has no newly supplied antecedent. The printed locators נג: and קנא: conventionally give 53b and 151b; no named witness was checked.
